clue.text: Shiny black article back in Italy

definitions.note: a phrase locating the answer, a city found in Italy

parts.note: raven-black hair is glossy and dark

indicators.note: sending a word back means reading it from its end to its start

parts.note: the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone describes a glossy black item they brought back from an Italian holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The article is turned round after the bird's colour to finish the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city in northern Italy famous for its Byzantine mosaics, so it is something found there.

clue.text: Anger about brother for instance is ludicrous

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps around it

parts.note: to rile is to anger
a brother is one example of a sibling, shortened to sib

explanation.surface: Getting angry about your brother, for example, is silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable or provoking ridicule, which is what ludicrous describes.

clue.text: Make sport of biology for a change

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in biology a sport is a mutant offshoot, an instance of this
second meaning: an alteration from the usual

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make sport of' looks like mocking biology, but a sport in biology is an organism that differs markedly from its parent type.
explanation.definitionFit: A variation is both a deviation in an organism from its type and, generally, any change or alteration.

clue.text: Milton bade her bring "Jest and youthful jollity"

definitions.text: Milton bade her bring "Jest and youthful jollity"

parts.note: surface reading: a poet giving orders to some woman
setter's reading: the quotation from L'Allegro, which begins 'Haste thee' addressing a spirit of nature

explanation.walkthrough: In Milton's poem L'Allegro the line runs 'Haste thee, ___, and bring with thee Jest and youthful Jollity'; the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem addresses a female nature spirit of classical myth, the one Milton calls upon to bring merriment.

clue.text: Add circumstantially to her rise — understand?

indicators.note: circum- means around, so this word goes around the other

parts.note: to append is to add

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tacks on extra details to her promotion and asks if you follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The upturned pronoun sits inside the verb after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend is to grasp mentally or perceive the meaning of something, a formal synonym of understand.

clue.text: Material for makeshift tea on Welsh river

indicators.note: something makeshift is improvised, so these letters are thrown together in a new arrangement

parts.note: the Taff flows through Cardiff
the letters of this drink rearranged

explanation.surface: A picnic by a Welsh river, with improvised tea brewed on the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the shuffled drink after the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven silk or synthetic fabric, a kind of cloth used for dresses.

clue.text: Summed up and put on record

definitions.meaning: first meaning: measured or assessed, as in 'I've got him sized up'
second meaning: recorded on magnetic tape

explanation.walkthrough: To have someone taped is British slang for having them fully figured out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both having a person weighed up thoroughly and recording sound on tape.

clue.text: Luxury garment the Russian promoted

parts.note: a fur coat
taken as written
a Red is a Soviet communist

explanation.surface: A Russian official is promoted and rewarded with a fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Red was the standard Cold War label for a Soviet Russian.
explanation.definitionFit: To further a cause is to advance or help it along, the same sense as promoting it.

clue.text: In France she meets a Pole

definitions.note: the answer is a woman's name

parts.note: the French pronoun for she
the North Pole

explanation.surface: A woman on holiday in France meets a Polish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France she' supplies the French word for she, and she also stands for the woman named.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a female given name, so a particular she is meant.

clue.text: It may make the truant conspicuous

definitions.text: It may make the truant conspicuous

parts.words: It may make the truant conspicuous
parts.note: surface reading: something that draws attention to a skiving pupil
setter's reading: the idiom 'conspicuous by one's not being there'

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'conspicuous by his ___': a truant is noticed precisely because he is not present.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant stays away from school, and not being there is the thing that gets him noticed.

clue.text: Harris's uncle's gone mad it's in the blood

indicators.note: a mind gone mad is disordered, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: Uncle Remus is the storyteller created by Joel Chandler Harris

explanation.surface: A family member has lost his mind, and it seems to be hereditary madness.
explanation.walkthrough: Joel Chandler Harris wrote the Uncle Remus tales of Brer Rabbit; the uncle's name is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Serum is the clear fluid part of blood left after clotting, so it is literally found in the blood.

clue.text: Tube has turnover of old Exchequer notes

parts.note: a pipe is a tube
something that rolls turns over and over

explanation.surface: A tube train company announces its turnover in old banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pipe Rolls were the annual financial records of the English Exchequer kept from the twelfth century onward.

clue.text: Sussex coast feature. No journey's end but an invasion area

indicators.note: saying no to a letter means taking it away from the word

parts.note: Beachy Head is a chalk headland near Eastbourne on the English south coast

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A tourist note on a famous cliff, oddly pivoting to a wartime landing.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the last letter of journey from BEACHY HEAD leaves BEACHHEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A beachhead is a defended position on a shore captured by invading troops as a base for further advance.

clue.text: Noah, changing direction, is found in China

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer, a province of China

indicators.note: a name that is changing gets its letters rearranged

parts.note: the name as written
north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Noah sails his ark off course and ends up in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing direction' looks like one phrase; changing shuffles Noah and direction supplies an extra letter for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Honan is the older romanisation of Henan, a province of central China.

clue.text: Lamb's prophet

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia
the possessive ending kept as written

explanation.walkthrough: Lamb is the essayist Charles Lamb, not an animal; his pen name plus the possessive gives the prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is the Greek form of Elijah, the Old Testament prophet, used in the New Testament.

clue.text: Brief inclination of select few

parts.note: brief means short
a ship's list is its lean

explanation.surface: A passing preference shown by an elite group.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortlist is the small group of candidates chosen from a larger field for final consideration.

clue.text: Sticking it out at point-to-point, ran into Benito

parts.note: two compass points, east and north, side by side

indicators.note: going into something places it inside that thing

parts.note: Benito Mussolini was Il Duce
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse racing report: a runner veered into a rider named Benito.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is an amateur steeplechase, but here it is two compass points joined. RAN goes inside Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to keep going through hardship, which is what sticking it out describes.

clue.text: Decide to discourage excavation

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
a mine is a dug-out pit

explanation.surface: Authorities resolve to put a stop to digging.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine is to settle or resolve a matter, the same as making a decision.

clue.text: Unremarkable reply?

parts.note: surface reading: dull or ordinary
setter's reading: an answer containing no remark at all

explanation.walkthrough: Unremarkable is read literally as 'without a remark', which is what this stock phrase to the press offers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard response of someone declining to say anything to questioners.

clue.text: Agreement to study about new road and type of junction

indicators.note: a new version of a word has its letters arranged afresh

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
c. for circa, about
the letters of this word rearranged
a T-junction

explanation.surface: Planners agree to survey a new road and decide what junction it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Circa, abbreviated c., is Latin for about; a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal treaty, especially one between the Vatican and a state, so it is a kind of agreement.

clue.text: With which to trim the ship?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cutting tool for hair or hedges
second meaning: a fast nineteenth-century sailing vessel

explanation.walkthrough: Trim the ship sounds like adjusting sails, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a shearing tool and a sleek fast sailing vessel such as the Cutty Sark.

clue.text: Darling birds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a homely British term of endearment, as in 'ta, love'

explanation.walkthrough: In northern and Midlands British speech the word is used to address someone fondly, much like darling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a familiar endearment in British English and the plural of a common waterbird.

clue.text: Got lost yesterday, confused when you once left

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into another order
something that has left is no longer there

parts.note: taken as written
ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off yesterday, bewildered after a companion departed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take Y and E out of yesterday, then rearrange the seven letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To have strayed is to have wandered away from the right path, that is to have gone astray.

clue.text: Means of access to fashionable tenancy …

parts.note: in fashion
a let is a rental arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting into a trendy rental property, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is an opening or passage by which something enters, such as a water or air intake.

clue.text: Record one century of sound reasoning

parts.note: a log is a record
Roman numeral one
C is a hundred

explanation.surface: A historian logs a single century of careful thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is the discipline of valid argument, the principles of correct thinking.

clue.text: … through previous executor

parts.note: per means by way of
former means earlier

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, access gained via an earlier executor of a will.
explanation.walkthrough: Executor suggests a will, but here it is one who executes, that is carries out, a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: One who executes a task or piece of music is a performer, someone who carries something out.

clue.text: Crowds footballers into eights?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crams or presses together
second meaning: rugby forwards, who form scrums of eight players

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby football the eight forwards are called the pack; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cramming people together and the groups of eight forwards in rugby teams.

clue.text: Overweight officer ordered to quarters

parts.note: an Officer of the Order of the British Empire
two compass quarters, south and east

explanation.surface: A portly officer is told to go to his quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour whose holders are officers of the Order; ordered nods to that.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes someone very fat, carrying far more body weight than is healthy.

clue.text: Operatic players

parts.note: surface reading: performers or musicians in an opera company
setter's reading: the travelling actors who give their name to a Leoncavallo opera

explanation.walkthrough: Leoncavallo's opera title means the clowns or strolling players, so the opera is named for its players.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian title of the opera refers to a troupe of commedia dell'arte actors at its centre.

clue.text: It's rough on this paper

parts.note: surface reading: a newspaper being hard on someone
setter's reading: the gritty abrasive coating sandpaper of this kind carries

explanation.walkthrough: The paper is an abrasive sheet, not a newspaper; the gritty mineral is what makes it rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a dark granular rock used as an abrasive powder glued onto paper or boards for smoothing.

clue.text: Rehearses ceremonies round the city district

indicators.note: going round something encloses it on both sides

parts.note: rites are ceremonies
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone practises ceremonial rituals around a city neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC (East Central).
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to repeat aloud from memory, as in rehearsing lines, so the verbs match in sense.

clue.text: Turned out always to spread new-mown grass

parts.note: ever means always
to ted is to spread cut grass out to dry as hay

explanation.surface: A farmer recalls always going out to spread the freshly cut hay.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is an old farming verb for scattering mown grass for drying.
explanation.definitionFit: Everted means turned inside out or outward, a technical term in anatomy and botany.
